cards.problem: Will Zn metal displace Cu²⁺ from CuSO₄(aq)? (Zn is above Cu in the activity series.)

steps.text: A more active metal reduces ions of a less active metal.
Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻; Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu. Net: Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu.

cards.answer: Yes — copper metal plates out; the blue Cu²⁺ colour fades.

cards.title: 4.1 General Properties of Metals, Reactivity Series, and Metallurgy
body: 4.1 General Properties of Metals, Reactivity Series, and Metallurgy

**Metals** are defined as electropositive chemical elements characterized by luster, high thermal and electrical conductivity, malleability, ductility, and the tendency to lose valence electrons to form positive cations in chemical reactions.

In the periodic table, metals occupy the left, center, and lower sections, constituting more than $$80\%$$ of all known elements. Physically, metals share several distinctive properties. In their pure state, they possess a shiny surface, a characteristic known as metallic luster. Most metals are dense, hard solids with high melting and boiling points, with mercury ($$Hg$$) being the sole liquid metal at room temperature. They are highly malleable (can be hammered or rolled into thin sheets) and ductile (can be drawn into thin wires). These properties are explained by metallic

cards.title: Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds
body: To organize metals systematically, they are arranged in order of their decreasing chemical activity to form the Reactivity (Activity) Series. Highly active alkali and alkaline earth metals (such as potassium, $$K$$, and sodium, $$Na$$) are placed at the top of the series because they react violently with cold water. Transition metals (such as zinc, $$Zn$$, and iron, $$Fe$$) are placed in the middle, reacting only with hot water or steam and dilute acids. Noble metals (such as copper, $$Cu$$, silver, $$Ag$$, and gold, $$Au$$) reside at the bottom of the series because they are chemically inert and do not react with water, steam, or dilute non-oxidizing acids.

cards.title: Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds
body: To enhance their properties, metals are often blended with other elements to form alloys. An alloy is a homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or a metal and a nonmetal. Alloying alters the physical properties of metals, typically increasing their hardness, tensile strength, and resistance to corrosion while decreasing their electrical conductivity and melting point. Common examples include brass (an alloy of copper and zinc), bronze (copper and tin), steel (iron and carbon), and stainless steel (iron, chromium, and nickel).

### 📝 Topic Challenge (Moderate to Hard)
1. Distinguish between minerals and ores, and explain if all minerals can be classified as ores.
*Answer:* A mineral is any naturally occurring element or compound found in the Earth's crust. An ore is a specific mineral from which a metal can be extracted profitably and economically. Therefore, all ores are minerals, but not all minerals are ores. If a mineral contains too low a concentration of a metal or is too expensive to process, it is not classified as an ore.

cards.problem: Which of the following metals is extracted industrially by the electrolysis of its molten chloride salt?

steps.text: **Step 1: Identify extraction methods based on reactivity**
Metals at the top of the activity series are highly reactive and extracted via electrolysis of molten salts.
Aluminum is extracted from its oxide (alumina, $$Al_2O_3$$). Sodium is extracted from its molten chloride ($$NaCl$$) in a Down's cell.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: Amphoteric oxides are unique because they possess the chemical capacity to react with:

steps.text: In chemistry, amphoteric substances can behave as both acids and bases.
An amphoteric oxide (like $$Al_2O_3$$ or $$ZnO$$) reacts with strong acids (behaving as a base) and with strong bases (behaving as an acid) to produce salts and water.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: The widely used industrial alloy brass is composed primarily of:

steps.text: Copper and tin form **bronze**. Iron and carbon form **steel**. Lead and tin form **solder**.
Brass is a homogeneous alloy composed primarily of copper and zinc.

cards.title: Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds
body: The Earth's crust is the major reservoir of metals. Naturally occurring elements or inorganic compounds found in the crust are called minerals. A mineral that contains a high percentage of a metal and from which the metal can be profitably and economically extracted is defined as an ore. While all ores are minerals, not all minerals are classified as ores. Highly reactive metals at the top of the activity series are never found free in nature; they always occur in combined form as oxides, chlorides, or silicates. Moderately reactive middle metals typically occur as sulfides, oxides, or carbonates. Least reactive metals at the very bottom of the series occur in their free, native metallic state.

> **💡 Did You Know?**: Sodium is so highly reactive with oxygen and water vapor in the air that it cannot be stored in standard containers. Instead, it must be kept completely submerged in kerosene or mineral oil to prevent it from spontaneously catching fire!

cards.problem: The principal ore of aluminum from which it is commercially extracted is:

steps.text: Hematite is the ore of iron ($$Fe_2O_3$$). Galena is the ore of lead ($$PbS$$).
Cryolite ($$Na_3AlF_6$$) is used as a solvent, but bauxite ($$Al_2O_3 \\cdot xH_2O$$) is the principal ore from which aluminum is commercially extracted.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: Sacrificial protection (galvanizing) of structural iron is achieved by coating it with a thin layer of:

steps.text: To protect iron sacrificed, we must coat it with a metal that is more reactive (higher in reactivity series) than iron.
Copper, gold, and lead are less reactive than iron. Zinc ($$Zn$$) is more reactive than iron.
Zinc corrodes preferentially to protect the underlying iron. Coating iron with zinc is specifically called galvanizing.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: What is the primary thermodynamic role of adding cryolite ($$Na_3AlF_6$$) to alumina ($$Al_2O_3$$) in the Hall-Héroult cell?

steps.text: Pure alumina has a melting point of $$2050^\circ\\text{C}$$, which is extremely expensive to maintain.
Dissolving alumina in molten cryolite lowers the melting point to about $$950^\circ\\text{C}$$. It also provides mobile ions ($$Na^+$$, $$AlF_6^{3-}$$) that enhance electrical conductivity.

cards.title: Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds
body: Chemically, metals are highly electropositive, meaning they tend to lose their valence electrons to achieve stable noble gas configurations ($$M \\rightarrow M^{n+} + ne^-$$). Metals react with oxygen in the air to produce basic metal oxides, although some metals form amphoteric oxides (such as aluminum oxide, $$Al_2O_3$$, and zinc oxide, $$ZnO$$) that can react with both acids and bases to produce salts and water. Highly active metals react vigorously with cold water to form metal hydroxides and release hydrogen gas, while less active metals require steam to form metal oxides and hydrogen. Active metals also react with dilute mineral acids to undergo single displacement reactions, displacing hydrogen gas and forming metal salts.

cards.title: Chemistry of Some Metals and Their Compounds
body: Extraction of these metals requires the science and technology of metallurgy. The metallurgical pathway involves three major phases: 1) Enrichment or concentration of the ore to remove unwanted sandy and rocky impurities, collectively known as gangue; 2) Chemical reduction of the concentrated ore to obtain crude metal; and 3) Refining or purification of the crude metal. The reduction method corresponds directly to the metal's position in the reactivity series. High-reactivity metals must be extracted via electrolytic reduction of their molten salts. Medium-reactivity metal sulfide and carbonate ores are first roasted (heated in excess air) or calcined (heated in limited air) to form metal oxides, which are then reduced using carbon (coke) at high temperatures. Low-reactivity metals are extracted by simply roasting their sulfide ores, followed by thermal reduction or heating alone.

cards.title: 4.2 Chemistry, Extraction, and Compounds of Key Representative Metals
body: 4.2 Chemistry, Extraction, and Compounds of Key Representative Metals

**Representative Metals** include the highly electropositive alkali metal Sodium, the post-transition metal Aluminum, and transition metals Iron, Copper, Zinc, and Gold, which have diverse extraction pathways (pyrometallurgy and electrometallurgy) and massive industrial utilities.

Sodium ($$Na$$) is highly reactive and is extracted by the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride in a Down's Cell. To lower the melting point of sodium chloride from $$801^\\circ\\text{C}$$ to about $$600^\\circ\\text{C}$$, calcium chloride ($$CaCl_2$$) is added as a flux. During electrolysis, sodium ions are reduced at the circular iron cathode: $$Na^+(l) + e^- \\rightarrow Na(l)$$, and chloride ions are oxidized at the central graphite anode: $$2Cl^-(l) \\rightarrow Cl_2(g) + 2e^-$$. cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: In a Blast Furnace, the primary chemical species acting as the reducing agent to convert iron ore to metallic iron is:

steps.text: Coke ($$C$$) burns to form $$CO_2$$, which reacts with excess coke to form carbon monoxide ($$CO$$).
While carbon (coke) is the original source, it is carbon monoxide ($$CO$$) gas that actually diffuses upwards and reduces the hematite ($$Fe_2O_3$$) solid to liquid iron.

cards.title: Study Notes worked
cards.problem: Which of the following metals is so chemically unreactive that it occurs primarily free in its native state in the Earth's crust?

steps.text: Sodium and aluminum are at the top (highly reactive). Iron is in the middle (moderately reactive). Gold is at the very bottom (noble/unreactive).
Because gold does not react with oxygen, water, or acids, it does not easily form compounds and is found free in its native metallic state.

why: Chalcopyrite (copper pyrites) CuFeS₂ is the main copper ore (textbook Table 4.2).

questions.q: In the reaction M(s) + 2HCl(aq) → H₂(g) + MCl₂(aq), M displaces hydrogen from the acid. M may stand for
why: Only metals above hydrogen in the activity series displace hydrogen from dilute acids.
Cu, Hg and Pt are below hydrogen; Zn is above it: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂. Answer: C.
